## Objectives

In this class we explore and describe three datasets. For this session We will:

- Compare datasets
- Merge different datasets

We start by importing the data from the previous sessions.

```{r initial settings}
# Import libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tableone)
library(here)

# Import data
cohort <- read_csv(here("data", "cohort_baseline_modified.csv"))
death <- read_csv(here("data", "death_followup_modified.csv"))
diagnoses <- read_csv(here("data", "registry_diagnoses_modified.csv"))
```

## 6. Merging the datasets

### 6.1 Preparing datasets

Do the datasets contain duplicated `person_id`?

*Hint: `duplicated()`*

```{r duplicates}
duplicated(cohort$person_id)
duplicated(diagnoses$person_id)
duplicated(death$person_id)
```

The `diagnoses` dataset contains repeated individuals, who have mroe than one diagnosis.

### 6.2 Remove duplicates

We will use only the first diagnosis reported in the table. Therefore, remove duplicated rows from the dataset.

```{r rem-duplicates}
diagnoses <- diagnoses %>%
  distinct(person_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

### 6.3 Merge

Make one dataset that keeps:

- all columns from the cohort dataset
- `diagnosis_code` from `diagnoses` dataset
- `died` from the `death` dataset

How many rows do you expect? How many do you get?

*Hint: start from the cohort and use `left_join()`.*

```{r merge}
merged <- cohort %>%
  left_join(diagnoses, by = "person_id") %>%
  left_join(death %>% select(person_id, died), by = "person_id")

nrow(merged)
```

### 6.4 Missing diagnosis codes

How many `NA`s are there in `diagnosis_code` now? What does `NA` mean in this dataset?

```{r merged-na}
sum(is.na(merged$diagnosis_code))

merged %>%
  filter(is.na(diagnosis_code)) %>%
  select(person_id)
```

There are 7 `NAs` which correspond to 7 individuals who do not have any IHD diagnosis in the registry.

### 6.5 Prevalent IHD among those who died

Did the people who died report prior (prevalent) IHD at baseline?

```{r ihd-death}
table(died = merged$died, ihd = merged$self_reported_prior_ihd)
```

None of them reported prior IHD at baseline.

### 6.6 Most common diagnosis by education

Among participants with secondary education, what was the most common diagnosis?

```{r secondary-education}
merged %>%
  filter(education == "Secondary") %>%
  count(diagnosis_code, sort = TRUE) %>%
  top_n(1)
```

I25.1 is the most common diagnosis amogn those with secondary educaiton.

## 6.6 Age and Diagnosis

What is the average age at which each IHD occurred among the individuals in the cohort? Build a `scatterplot` with the mean age for each diagnosis.

```{r}
age_diagnosis <- merged %>%
  group_by(diagnosis_code) %>%
  summarise(age_mean = mean(age),
            count = n()) %>%
  na.omit()

ggplot(age_diagnosis, aes(x = diagnosis_code, y = age_mean, size = count))+
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()
```

By weighting the points by size we can observe that a lot of the codes had only one observation, which should make us skeptical about the calculated mean age.

## 7. Save merged dataset

Save your merged dataset in your local folder

```{r save dataset}
write_csv(merged, here("data", "merged_dataset.csv"))
```
